## supervisor stephen sherrill
San Francisco is a city on the rise and we must keep that momentum going.
As a father raising a family in District 2 with my wife Sarah, I want this to be the place where families and businesses choose to start, stay, and grow.
I focus on the basics: safe streets, clean neighborhoods, and thriving small businesses. I know how to get things done at City Hall, and every result I deliver starts with showing up in our neighborhoods and listening.
San Francisco has long been a beacon of freedom and democratic values. To protect those values, we need to win on everyday issues. I'm working to make San Francisco easier to live in and easier to raise a family in, a city that inspires pride and possibility.
We're moving forward. Our best days are ahead, and I'm not letting up. I hope you'll join me.
Learn More

Delivering for D2
###### Public Safety & Clean Streets
Safe, clean neighborhoods are the foundation of our city’s future.
###### what we have done
Brought seven-day-a-week police foot patrols to the Marina
Protected funding for street cleaning, trash pickup, and park maintenance
Voted to appoint 3 new pro-safety police commissioners
###### what's Next
Stronger police response to drug activity near schools and playgrounds
Expand fentanyl prevention and abstinence-based recovery programs
More trash cans and security technology across every neighborhood
View More
###### thriving SMALL BUSINESSES
Strong small businesses mean strong neighborhoods.
###### what we have done
Extended First Year Free to waive fees for new businesses opening in SF
Removed outdated restrictions on Van Ness to help fill empty storefronts
Led the Clay Theatre legislation and introduced the Union Street entertainment zone
###### what's next
Keep cutting red tape so it is faster and cheaper to open a business in SF
Advance the Fillmore entertainment zone and create more opportunities for our businesses to engage commercial corridors
Push for commonsense reforms that let neighborhood businesses attract customers
Push to make parking work better for businesses and customers across our commercial corridors
View More
###### a san francisco that works for you
From fixing sidewalks to championing neighborhood projects, Stephen's office is here to deliver. He believes the best ideas come from the community, and he takes pride in being accessible and responsive to every resident of District 2. More trees near Laurel Village? Holiday lights at the Palace of Fine Arts? Your ideas make our neighborhoods great.

## Latest Developments
NEWS ARTICLE
#### S.F. closer to delaying controversial $300K sprinkler mandate for high-rise condos
Under the new legislation, the 9,800 units covered by the sprinkler ordinance — most of them in Nob Hill, Russian Hill, the Marina and Telegraph Hill — would have until 2032, instead of 2027, to obtain permits for the sprinkler work, which some home owners associations have estimated would cost between $200,000 and $300,000 per unit.
The legislation was co-sponsored by Supervisors Danny Sauter and Stephen Sherrill, whose district comprises most of the impacted buildings.
Read more

#### SF could make it easier for movie theaters to sell alcoholic drinks
The Board of Supervisors unanimously gave Sherrill’s idea an initial nod Tuesday.
Sherrill is pushing legislation to make it easier for movie houses to sell alcohol if they are licensed to do so, and also to simplify the process for movie houses to offer other types of cultural attractions.
He said his proposed ordinance emerged from the ongoing effort to reopen the historic Clay Theatre in Pacific Heights.
Read more

#### Wealthy S.F. neighborhood’s 700-unit housing development to break ground
3333 California St, the former 10-acre UCSF campus is slated to eventually be home to 744 housing units, a 175-spot child care facility, about 40,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space, and 5 acres of open space.
3700 California St. a few blocks to the west on the former California Pacific Medical Center campus that closed in 2019. That project will generate up to 19 new residential buildings with up to 530 homes.
